query: What review signals predict negative Amazon product satisfaction?

per_column.name: negative_sentiment_words
per_column.rationale: A count of negative sentiment terms directly targets the negative-satisfaction query and gives a genuine modeling axis. Values are broadly grounded, though the lexicon appears crude (AMZ-0003 with clearly negative content scored 0), suggesting some miss/mismatch but no invented facts.

per_column.name: positive_sentiment_words
per_column.rationale: Complementary contrast signal useful for predicting satisfaction. Grounded in text but the lexicon is imperfect (AMZ-0004, a glowing review, scored 0 positives), indicating undercounting rather than fabrication.

per_column.name: allcaps_word_count
per_column.rationale: Emphasis/shouting is a plausible stylistic predictor of strong (often negative) affect. Values are mechanically derivable from text and samples look consistent, though acronyms like 'DVD' may inflate counts.

per_column.name: exclamation_mark_count
per_column.rationale: Punctuation-intensity feature offering some analytical leverage on affect intensity. Trivially and reliably derivable from source text.

per_column.name: question_mark_count
per_column.rationale: Rhetorical questioning can correlate with frustration/complaint, giving modest leverage. Fully derivable from text; samples match.

per_column.name: repeated_punctuation_count
per_column.rationale: Repeated punctuation (e.g. '...', '!!!') captures emotional intensity, a reasonable predictor. Directly countable from text; sample values plausible.

per_column.name: title_word_count
per_column.rationale: A bare length/token-count feature with weak, generic link to satisfaction; low analytical leverage for this query. Values are exactly derivable and correct.

per_column.name: content_word_count
per_column.rationale: Raw length is a generic feature with limited but nonzero value (review length can weakly relate to sentiment). Perfectly grounded token count.

per_column.name: comparative_language_count
per_column.rationale: Comparative phrasing ('worse than', 'only one') is a meaningful evaluative signal. Reasonably grounded, though the lexicon is sparse (mostly zeros) and hard to fully verify from samples.

per_column.name: investment_complaint_words
per_column.rationale: Price/value complaint terms are a relevant satisfaction axis. But AMZ-0005 ('costs more...but well worth it') scored 1, catching a price mention that is actually POSITIVE, showing the feature detects topic not complaint polarity, weakening groundedness of the 'complaint' framing.

per_column.name: product_failure_words
per_column.rationale: Failure/defect terms are strong predictors of negative satisfaction and a genuine grouping axis. Mostly zero and plausibly grounded, though verification is limited by sparse positive samples.

per_column.name: durability_complaint_words
per_column.rationale: Durability complaints are a specific, useful negative-satisfaction signal. Values are keyword-derivable and appear grounded, with no observed contradictions in samples.

judge.rationale: Most columns provide genuine, distinct axes (sentiment counts, emphasis/punctuation intensity, complaint-topic detectors) directly relevant to predicting negative satisfaction. A few (title_word_count, content_word_count) are generic length features with weak leverage. Values are largely mechanically or lexically derivable from the source text with no invented facts; groundedness is dented only by imperfect lexicons that mis-detect polarity (e.g., investment_complaint firing on a positive price mention, sentiment lexicons missing clearly affective rows). No confident fabrication observed.
